notes.6: Many candidates understood the correct method for working out the actual diameter of the cell. Candidates would benefit from being able to recall and apply the formula for calculating magnification.
notes.7: Most candidates knew that diffusion is involved and that a partially permeable membrane is required for osmosis to occur. Some candidates incorrectly thought that cell walls were required for osmosis to occur.
notes.8: This proved to be a very demanding question. Osmosis would cause water to pass through the partially permeable membrane of both pieces of apparatus and so the liquid level in both tubes would rise.
notes.10: This proved to be a very demanding question. To select the correct option, candidates were required to work through the information on the graph and determine which statement was correct. A methodical approach allowed successful candidates to select option D.
notes.12: There was some uncertainty as to whether the answer was photosynthesis or respiration. Photosynthesis in the spiral-shaped chloroplasts releases oxygen and that oxygen attracts the bacteria.
notes.13: Many candidates appreciated that nitrates are required to make amino acids which can then be used to make proteins. Starch was a common incorrect response.
notes.14: Many candidates did not know that assimilation is the stage of nutrition taking place when food molecules become part of a body cell. The most common incorrect answer was A, absorption.
notes.15: This was a demanding question with successful candidates being able to identify absorption and digestion as the two processes represented by the experiment.
notes.17: Whilst most candidates understood that water first enters root hair cells, many candidates were uncertain whether water then progresses to the xylem or to the mesophyll. The correct route was root hair to xylem to mesophyll.
notes.18: Most candidates incorrectly believed that a function of phloem is to transport minerals to the roots.
notes.22: Many candidates correctly identified where the carbon dioxide concentration was the highest.
notes.24: Many candidates incorrectly thought that the amount of urea in the blood increases as it passes through the kidneys. The liver is responsible for producing urea from excess amino acids whereas the kidneys are responsible for removing urea from the blood.
notes.25: There was some uncertainty in the location of relay neurones. Few candidates could recall that relay neurones are located in the spinal cord.
notes.27: Many candidates successfully selected option D. Candidates were uncertain as to the effect of adrenaline on the size of the pupils and therefore option C was frequently selected. Adrenaline increases the size of the pupils.
notes.29: There was uncertainty by many candidates about the part of the flower that receives the pollen nucleus during fertilisation. The pollen nucleus is received by the ovule.
notes.31: Many candidates were unaware that the diaphragm is a barrier method of birth control.
notes.32: Many candidates were not aware of the features of mitosis. Perhaps some candidates confused mitosis with meiosis.
notes.36: Interpreting the food web proved to be demanding for some candidates. Successful candidates appreciated that organism L was a decomposer.
notes.37: To be successful, candidates needed to work through the diagram methodically, applying their knowledge of the carbon cycle to the diagram. Plants give out carbon dioxide during respiration and animals ingest plants when feeding.
notes.general_comments: There was good understanding of: the characteristics of living things; the type of organisms that cause tooth decay; what a transmissible disease is, and the effects of deforestation. There was some uncertainty about: the functions of phloem; the stages of human nutrition; where urea is produced in the body; the structure that receives the pollen nucleus during fertilisation; what are barrier methods of birth control, and the features of mitosis. It is important for candidates to work methodically through information provided in questions, such as Questions 8, 10, 12, 22, 37 and 40.
